title: [30/9/2023] - Fitness membership numbers across different age groups in an Asian country
prompt: The chart displays information about fitness membership numbers across different age groups in an Asian country from 1970 to 2000. Summarize the key information by highlighting the main features and make appropriate comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart gives information about the numbers of fitness memberships among individuals of 3 different age groups from 1970 to 2000.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while fitness memberships of those from 18 to 35 displayed a trend of instability, those of people both under 18 and from 36 to 65 gradually rose over time. In addition, the young adult age group recorded the highest membership numbers for most of the given period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: With regard to individuals in the 18-35 age group, its members numbered just over 2,000 in 1970. In the subsequent years, after an initial surge to 4,000 in 1975, membership receded to its original level of just over 2,000 in 1990. This was followed by another larger surge to a peak of 5000 members in 1995, before declining again to 4,000 five years later.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the other two age groups, there were 1,000 members under 18 in 1970, double the figure for 36-to-65-year-olds. Thereafter, the number of gym members under 18 varied over the following 2 decades, from approximately 1,800 to 2,800, until 1990, when it began its ascent to a high of 3,500 by the end of the period. Likewise, membership among the oldest bracket also maintained a steady upward trend, but without any fluctuations, ending up at 2,700 in the year 2000.
